title: Microsoft Purview: audit logs for OCR transactions in Exchange and Teams
notes: claim 52: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing overstates gaps in OCR audit documentation; Microsoft already describes related record schemas and general audit retention rules. It also makes unverified promises that OCR settings do not affect logging and that scanning charges will not change.

claims.claim: OCR scanning needs an Azure pay-as-you-go subscription and billing set up through Microsoft Syntex.
claims.quote: To use OCR scanning, your organization's Global admin needs to verify that an Azure pay-as-you-go subscription is in place. To use OCR, set up Microsoft Syntex pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: The Global admin can set up OCR billing.
claims.quote: Because it's an optional feature, your Global admin must set up pay-as-you-go billing to enable OCR.

claims.claim: The Compliance admin configures tenant OCR settings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls: row 1
claims.claim: Tenant OCR location settings are in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Optical character recognition (OCR).
claims.quote: Select Settings. Select Optical character recognition (OCR) to enter your OCR configuration settings. Select the locations where you want to scan images. Select the groups that you want included or excluded from OCR scans.
claims.fix: Keep the path, which reaches the correct configuration page, and add to row 1's note: 'Select the locations where you want to scan images and the groups to include or exclude.'

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for these tenant-level OCR location settings.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The general unified audit switch governs audit availability, and turning auditing off makes portal audit searches return no results.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: SMB licences do not have auditing enabled by default and require manual enablement.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium. In both these cases, you must manually enable auditing for your organization.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published an OCR-audit-record-specific tier or licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview OCR audit records licensing Audit Standard Premium retention ComplianceExchangeOcr CdpOcrBilling. Read audit overview, Purview service description, OCR overview and both Graph OCR types; product licences are stated, but no OCR-event-specific tier is named.

claims.claim: Neither the OCR overview nor the audit overview publishes a separate meter for OCR audit logs.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview OCR audit logs separate billing meter price retention license. Read OCR and audit overviews; OCR scanning is metered, but neither names a separate OCR-audit-log meter. Purview billing search excerpt meters non-Microsoft generative AI interactions, not OCR.

claims.claim: Audit (Standard) retains current records for 180 days.
claims.quote: In Audit (Standard), the system retains records for 180 days, which means you can search for activities that occurred within the past six months.

claims.claim: Audit retention and searchability depend on the subscription and licences assigned to users.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Open questions
claims.claim: Which retention applies to OCR audit records is not yet published.
claims.quote: Audit records generated by non-user entities (such as service principal actions, system events, and application activities) are retained for a fixed period of one year. This retention period isn't configurable and custom audit log retention policies don't apply to these records.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket retention gap with: 'Published unified-audit retention rules depend on the record's workload, originating identity and licensing. Non-user entity records have fixed one-year retention; Audit (Standard) user records have 180-day retention. Microsoft has not identified this roadmap item's originating identity or record mapping.' Keep the existing subscription-dependent statement and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-solutions-overview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described what an OCR audit record contains.
claims.quote: The audit data for this record type is returned as the auditData property in an auditLogRecord. dynamicProperties | microsoft.graph.security.auditRecordTypeDictionary | Inherited from auditData.
claims.fix: Replace the broad content gap with: 'Graph documents related OCR audit types with an auditData payload containing dynamicProperties, but does not enumerate their event-specific dynamic fields or link them to this roadmap item.' Keep the advice to inspect a sample, and use the same narrower gap in Why it matters. The cited Graph OCR pages and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/security-auditrecordtypedictionary?view=graph-rest-1.0 support this wording.

claims.claim: Audit searches can be filtered by workload and individual records can be opened for their details.
claims.quote: Workloads: Enter or search for workload services to search for activity related to the selected workloads. Select a specific activity to see more details about the activity in a fly-out window.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: row 1 and closing prose
claims.claim: Tenant OCR settings do not change whether transactions are logged or what is logged.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview OCR tenant settings control whether transactions audit logged logging disable. Read OCR overview, audit enable/disable and both Graph OCR types; no passage states that tenant OCR settings cannot affect logging or logged contents.
claims.fix: Replace row 1's note sentence 'This controls OCR scanning, not whether OCR transactions are logged' with 'This controls OCR scanning.' Remove 'and do not change what is logged' from the closing Governance controls paragraph. Do not infer the interaction between the OCR setting and the new logging feature.

claims.claim: OCR scanning billing does not change with this item.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview OCR audit logs separate billing meter price retention license; "OCR" "audit" "transaction" Purview. Read roadmap, OCR and audit overviews and Graph OCR types; none promises unchanged OCR scanning billing when this item arrives.
claims.fix: Remove ', and that does not change with this item' from the cost rationale. Keep the documented statement that OCR scanning uses Azure pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining OCR scanning consumption billing with Audit subscription requirements.
claims.quote: To use OCR, set up Microsoft Syntex pay-as-you-go billing. After you enter billing information in Microsoft Syntex, your Compliance admin can configure OCR in Microsoft Purview without any extra setup or licensing requirements.
claims.fix: Retain mixed only with this clarifying sentence in licensing.notes: 'The mixed model describes OCR scanning's Azure billing prerequisite and existing Audit subscription requirements, not a published separate charge or OCR-event-specific entitlement for this roadmap item.' Keep the existing statement that the OCR-event-specific audit tier is unpublished.
